subject: history_social
passage: The Phoenicians, seafaring traders based along the eastern coast of the Mediterranean, used an alphabet of just twenty-two letters. Unlike many earlier writing systems, it did not require hundreds of different signs. Their alphabet, which recorded only ______ adapted by the Greeks, who added letters for vowels. The Greek version, in turn, became an ancestor of the Latin alphabet used to write English today.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject "Their alphabet" goes with the verb "was adapted." In between, "which recorded only consonants" is extra information. It opens with a comma after "alphabet," so it must close with a comma before "was."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon would cut the subject "Their alphabet" off from its verb, leaving two fragments.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Extra information that opens with a comma can't close with a dash; the two marks must match.
explanation.C: Correct. The closing comma matches the comma after "alphabet," so the subject connects to "was adapted."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the extra information runs into the verb, and "consonants was" seems to pair a plural noun with a singular verb.
